newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr drifts up vs yen in Tokyo on mark/yen buying.
newsitem.headline: Dlr drifts up vs yen in Tokyo on mark/yen buying.

text.p: ASIAN FOREX ACTIVITY:
0005 GMT
*Dollar drifted higher against yen but eased versus mark in early Tokyo trade, mainly due to mark/yen short-covering.
*Some operators may have decided to square mark/yen shorts for now as test of 1.80 marks to dollar seems difficult during Tokyo trading hours, a city bank trader said.
*Absence of fresh incentives expected to keep dollar/yen in tight range, with its upside seen heavy due to Japanese exporter offers above 114.20 yen, while downside seen solid near 113 yen.
*"A lot of people expect the mark/yen to test 63 yen eventually. But the dollar's rise above 1.80 marks would be prerequisite for this," said the city bank trader.
*Mark stood at around 63.62/65 yen at 0013 GMT, compared with around 63.49 yen in New York late Monday.
*Expectations of commercial dollar buying at 0100 GMT fixing are also helping to underpin greenback, traders said.
*Bargain-hunting dollar buying interest by some institutional investors is expected near 113 yen, traders said.
*Dollar closed at 113.95/05 yen and 1.7950/60 marks in New York on Monday.
*Dollar twice charged towards 1.80 marks in New York overnight, but stopped just shy of the key level.
*Traders said dollar could test 1.80 marks again when European markets open later Tuesday, but they are cautious that German officials might repeat comments expressing worries about mark's weakness.
*Overnight wire story was said to have quoted an anonymous Bundesbank official as saying Buba was concerned with dollar above 1.75 marks, but not enough to intervene to support mark.
*Traders in Europe also said on Monday that Bank of Italy had bought mark/lira at 970, boosting mark from six-month low.
*There were also rumours overnight that other authorities had also intervened to bolster mark, including Scandinavian central banks.
*Tokyo players may remain reluctant to push dollar/yen in either direction ahead of news briefing by senior finance ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara at 6.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).

*Sakakibara, who currently heads MOF's International Finance Bureau, will hold a news conference after his official appointment as new vice finance minister for international affairs. Outgoing MOF vice minister for international affairs, Takatoshi Kato, will also attend.

*"Dollar/yen could just remain trapped in a tight range during Tokyo trading hours. People may take a wait-and-see stance until trade data in Japan and the United States is released later this week," said a trader at a trust bank.
*Japan's customs-cleared trade balance for June will be released on Thursday while U.S. international trade data for May is due on Friday.
-- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
